equivalents.why: The numeric value of `AngleSourceKind::None` is not part of any promise. Every site compares by name, `reading_` is explicitly initialized with the enumerators by name, and nothing in the library casts this enum to an integer or writes it to a record -- which is exactly why `board_record.hpp` pins `BoardItem` with a `static_assert` and this one is left alone: that value *is* encoded, this one is not. Pinning it here would create a promise nobody consumes.

Same for `AngleQuality::Ok`. Note that `Ok = 0` *would* be a dangerous zero value if a zero-initialized reading were ever observable, which is why the member is initialized explicitly (`reading_{0, 0, Blind, None, NaN, 0}`) and why `reading()` before the first step answers `Blind`. The mutant moves the numbering behind that explicit initialization, so nothing can see it.

`if (count > kMaxOffers) count = kMaxOffers;` -- at `count == kMaxOffers` both forms assign the value the variable already holds, so the clamp is a no-op on both sides of the boundary. The interesting off-by-one next to it (`count == 0` widened to `count == 1`) was a real blind spot and now has a case: `OneOfferIsStillAnOffer`.

A zero-length step is already a no-op in the arithmetic: `max_change_rad_s = accel * 0 = 0`, so the ramp re-assigns the velocity it had, and `position += 0.5 * (v + v) * 0 = 0`. The guard exists for `dt_s < 0` and `NaN`, and the mutation touches neither. The `dt_s == 0` case *is* covered -- `NumbersThatCannotDescribeAMoveAreRefusedAndNothingMoves` steps with it -- so what this says is that the mutant cannot be distinguished, not that nothing looks.

The sign chosen for a zero remaining distance is unobservable. At `remaining == 0`, `ahead_rad` is `-(|v| * dt) <= 0`, so `stop_speed` is 0 and `wanted = +-0`; both signs drive the ramp identically (the comparisons are against +-0, which compare equal), and the landing test needs `position >= target` with `direction > 0` or `position <= target` with `direction < 0`, which at `position == target` are both true. The reading after that step is the target, zero speed, done -- either way.
`(ahead_rad > 0.0) ? ahead_rad : 0.0` -- at `ahead_rad == 0` both arms yield `0.0`, which is the whole point of the conditional.

At `wanted == velocity + max_change` the first arm does `velocity += max_change` and the else arm assigns `wanted`; both are `velocity_rad_s_ + max_change_rad_s`, computed from the same two doubles, so the assignment is the same number. The ramp is "clamp to one acceleration step", and equality is inside the clamp either way.
Same as line 213 in the other direction: at equality both arms assign `velocity_rad_s_ - max_change_rad_s`.

`direction` is only ever `+1` or `-1` -- it is assigned by `(remaining_rad > 0.0) ? 1.0 : -1.0` and nothing else -- so `direction > 0.0` and `direction >= 0.0` are the same predicate on every value the variable can hold. This is not an unprobed boundary: the value cannot be zero.
Same for `direction < 0.0` and `direction <= 0.0`: `direction` is +-1 by construction.

_comment: Mutation scores as measured by mutate.py, one entry per module, with the exact file set and limit used.
Stage 2 of the maturity plan records these numbers without setting a target: a threshold chosen before
the first measurement is a number picked to be met. The gate refuses a drop of more than
5 points and refuses a module with no entry at all.
`survivors` is the work list: each one is either a blind spot in the tests or an equivalent mutant, and
only a human can say which -- a survivor classified as equivalent is not deleted, it is explained.
